title: View Traversal: Measure, Layout, Draw, and Invalidation Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies view traversal: measure, layout, draw, and invalidation?
options: Use measure for constrained size, layout for bounds, draw for visuals, and request only the invalidation scope the change requires.
Call requestLayout for every color change
questions.answer: Use measure for constrained size, layout for bounds, draw for visuals, and request only the invalidation scope the change requires.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: invalidate always forces the entire hierarchy to run measure and layout again.
questions.explanation: Calling requestLayout for a color-only change schedules geometry work that invalidate alone could handle.

questions.prompt: When is requestLayout required instead of only invalidate?
questions.answer: When a change can affect measured size or child positioning and therefore requires a new geometry traversal.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
